title: Simhika
hook: three meetings over the sea, three different answers, and then the far shore

segments.voice: Yesterday: Simhika seized his shadow and dragged him down, until he looked below and knew her.

A good doctor doesn't treat every patient the same way. Knowing which response a moment needs is a skill all its own. Over one stretch of sea, Hanuman has now met three beings. One offered him rest. One tested him. And one, Simhika, wants to swallow him whole. Same monkey, same crossing, same water. Watch how differently he answers each.
screen: `WHICH RESPONSE DOES THIS NEED?` → `REST, A TEST, A THREAT.`

segments.voice: Simhika opens her mouth wide, and at first Hanuman does what worked with Surasa. He makes himself huge, and she opens wider. Then he makes himself small and drops straight into her mouth. But this time he doesn't dart back out with a bow. Inside her, Valmiki says, he tears at her vital organs with his nails, then shoots out again, quick as thought. Simhika falls dead into the sea. The beings watching from the sky cheer, and they give him a line worth keeping: whoever has, as you do, four things, steadiness, insight, intelligence and skill, does not fail at the work. Set the three meetings side by side. Mainaka offered a gift, and Hanuman answered with courtesy: a touch of the hand, a thank-you, and onward. Surasa set a test from the gods, and he answered with wit: smaller, not bigger, both promises kept. Simhika was simply a danger, and he answered with force, quickly and completely. Same Hanuman, three different responses. That's the four in action: steadiness to stay on course, insight to see what each thing really is, intelligence to choose the move, skill to carry it out. Then he looks ahead and sees it at last: the far shore. Trees, a line of hills, and beyond them a city. He comes down on a mountain at the water's edge, and Valmiki notes that after a hundred yojanas, he isn't even out of breath.
screen: `INTO THE MOUTH, AND OUT AGAIN.` · `STEADINESS, INSIGHT, MIND, SKILL.` · `COURTESY, WIT, FORCE.` · then, large: `THE FAR SHORE.`

segments.voice: Think back over yesterday and find three moments that asked something different of you: one that needed kindness, one cleverness, one firmness. For each, notice what you actually gave, with no grading. Then let the breath come and go, steady, as Hanuman lands without being out of breath.
Simhika. The shadow-catcher whom Hanuman defeats from the inside, the third of three meetings over the sea, each answered in a different way.
Your line: steadiness, insight, intelligence and skill. Ahead, a city waits for nightfall. Day six hundred eleven, done.

howItsDone: Readers of the Sundara Kanda often point to the verse about steadiness, insight, intelligence and skill as a summary of Hanuman's character.

fork.setup: you're Hanuman. Simhika has opened her mouth wide to swallow you. you've already beaten a mouth like this once. what do you do?
options: bow and ask permission to pass.
shrink, dive in, and destroy her from inside.
fork.reveal: he becomes small, drops into her mouth, tears her vital organs, and flies out. Simhika falls into the sea.

original.note: Sanskrit dhṛti, steadiness: the first of the four qualities praised after Simhika's defeat.

trapdoor: what you thought: Simhika is just the same test as Surasa again.
what it means: she's a real danger, and Hanuman's answer is different: quick and final.
what a scholar hears: the verse naming dhṛti, dṛṣṭi, mati and dākṣya (steadiness, insight, intelligence, skill) is spoken by the beings in the sky as praise of Hanuman himself.
recall: the ascetic who waited long for Rama
a finger-ring with Rama's name on it

chat.says: Hanuman bowed to Surasa but killed Simhika. Why treat them so differently?
options: Surasa was the gods' test; Simhika was just a danger out to eat him.
He'd used up all his patience on Surasa and had none left.
Simhika had insulted Rama, so he wanted to punish her.
chat.meaning: Hanuman read each meeting for what it was: courtesy for a gift, wit for a test, force for a real threat.

Simhika.meaning: a demoness in the southern sea who catches creatures by their shadows

Surasa.meaning: the serpent mother who tested Hanuman and blessed him

Mainaka.meaning: the golden mountain that rose from the sea to offer rest

yojanas.meaning: an old Indian measure of distance, many miles each

Valmiki.meaning: the poet-sage traditionally credited with the Ramayana

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 1 (Simhika's defeat; the four qualities; arrival on the shore)

notes: The four-qualities verse (dhṛti, dṛṣṭi, mati, dākṣya): confirm that it is spoken by the beings in the sky after Simhika's death (and not after Surasa), and the exact terms.
Hanuman lands on a mountain on Lanka's shore (Lamba, a peak of Trikuta, in Sundara 1–2); confirm. 'Not out of breath': confirm.
The gift/test/threat framing is the script's own reading; confirm the Keeper is comfortable with it.
